raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-MEX-SustainableValueChains",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "NAFIN faces potential foreign exchange risk on its balance sheet when providing local currency (MXN) sub-loans financed by international loan proceeds.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Manage foreign exchange risk on NAFIN's balance sheet using Mexico's currency swap market and restrict foreign currency sub-loans to exported-oriented firms with natural hedges.",
      "evidence": "NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s well developed currency swap market."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Default by beneficiary enterprises or participating financial institutions could cause credit losses for NAFIN and financial intermediaries.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Enforce strict financial intermediary eligibility criteria, single-borrower exposure caps, and mandate minimum co-financing levels from beneficiary enterprises and PFIs.",
      "evidence": "NAFIN will assume the credit risk of the BEs when lending directly and of the PFIs on second-tier operations"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "High transaction costs, MRV complexity, and limited internal capacity of SMEs and mid-caps may result in low loan uptake and demand.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Deploy grant-funded technical assistance under Component 2 to support feasibility studies, build borrower capacity, and offset sustainability plan verification costs.",
      "evidence": "risk of a situation where financing is available, but uptake is limited."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Participating financial institutions may lack sufficient technical capacity to originate, appraise, and monitor green loans and sustainability-linked financial products.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide dedicated technical assistance, training, standardized evaluation templates, and digital monitoring systems to PFI teams under Component 2.",
      "evidence": "Mexican financial institutions are limited in their capacity to design, originate, appraise and monitor green loans and sustainable finance products."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Weak or unverified Key Performance Indicators and Sustainability Performance Targets could lead to greenwashing and loss of product credibility.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Require ex-ante validation and ex-post verification of company Sustainability Plans and targets by qualified independent entities.",
      "evidence": "To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets and results in the SP will be subject to... ex-ante validation and ex-post verification"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "NAFIN staff's lack of direct experience conducting World Bank procurement processes could cause contracting delays under Component 2.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Appoint a designated qualified procurement professional to NAFIN's project team and conduct hands-on World Bank training during early implementation.",
      "evidence": "while NAFIN staff are familiar with the World Bank Procurement Regulations, they have not been directly involved in carrying out selection and contracting processes."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Reliance on legacy IT information systems requiring manual data consolidation creates financial management efficiency constraints and reporting risks.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Enforce standardized reporting templates in the POM, mandate supervisory review procedures, and establish robust reconciliation protocols.",
      "evidence": "The main residual FM risks relate to efficiency constraints arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual consolidation"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Severe weather hazards like heatwaves, droughts, and floods could disrupt beneficiary enterprise operations and lower business productivity.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Integrate climate resilience screening into sub-project evaluations and prioritize financing for resilience-enhancing, water-saving, and energy-reliable technologies.",
      "evidence": "Mexico faces significant climate vulnerability due to its exposure to extreme weather events such as heatwaves, droughts, hurricanes, and floods"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Persistent gender gaps and lower credit access rates for women entrepreneurs could lead to the exclusion of women-led businesses from project financing.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish transparent access criteria, launch targeted communication campaigns, and track disbursements using dedicated gender-inclusive results indicators.",
      "evidence": "women-led businesses face persistent barriers to financing: only 46 percent have ever sought credit compared to 50 percent of firms nationally"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Subprojects funded via financial intermediaries may cause adverse environmental and social impacts if ESMS frameworks are inconsistently applied.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Enforce a project Exclusion List excluding high E&S risk subprojects, require due diligence for Category A/B credits, and perform periodic World Bank sample supervision.",
      "evidence": "Environmental and Social (E&S) risk is assessed as Substantial, considering the nature of the financial instruments to be used and the structure of the operation."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Mexican suppliers failing to adopt clean technologies risk forward-exclusion from global value chains as multinational anchor companies enforce Scope 3 ESG targets.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Partner with large anchor corporations and industry associations to build supplier pipelines and provide targeted long-term green and sustainability-linked sub-loans.",
      "evidence": "Firms that do not comply risk forward-exclusion from supply chains, with implications for sales and employment"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "High national dependence on fossil fuels and elevated energy intensity expose Mexican manufacturing enterprises to energy-transition risks and price volatility.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Mandate that at least 50% of SLL portfolio GHG reductions stem from energy measures and at least 40% of the Green Loan portfolio finances clean energy technologies.",
      "evidence": "marked by high dependence on fossil fuels, exposure to price volatility, and persistent inefficiency."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Delays in fulfilling legal effectiveness conditions, including POM and Sustainable Finance Framework adoption, could delay project startup.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Utilize grant resources from the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) to advance document preparation prior to loan effectiveness.",
      "evidence": "The Additional Conditions of Effectiveness consist of the following: ... adoption of POM and Sustainable Finance Framework"
    }
  ]
}

risks.evidence: NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s well developed currency swap market.
